- issue_comment created in `venue-repo`#2 ("Widths and smallest type size for figures and tables") by `venue-repo`  > NeurIPS 2026 Main Track, submission mode; details and sources in \`VENUE.md\` §2 of this repository.
  > - Text width **5.5 in** (one column; there is no separate column width). Block 9 in high; US Letter. Figures: at most 5.5 in wide (\`width=<k>\linewidth\`); two side-by-side panels about 2.65 in each. Figures may not go into the margins or exceed the text block.
  > - Main-text limit: **9 pages including all figures and tables**; references, appendix and checklist are outside it.
  > - Smallest type: the venue sets **no minimum for figure text**. The style floors \`\footnotesize\` at 8 pt, \`\scriptsize\` at 7 pt, \`\tiny\` at 6 pt. Recommendation: figure text at least **7 pt as printed (8 pt preferred)**, so size figures at their final printed width and do not rely on scaling. Tables: \`\small\` (9 pt) or \`\footnotesize\` (8 pt); nothing smaller. Captions print at body size (10 pt), set by the style; do not change it.
  > - Fonts: Type 1 or embedded TrueType only; Type 3 and non-embedded fonts get flagged. Set \`pdf.fonttype: 42\` (and \`ps.fonttype: 42\`) in matplotlib; vector PDF preferred.
  > - Conventions: caption after a figure, title before a table; \`booktabs\`, no vertical rules; caption lower case except first word and proper nouns; the caption says what the figure shows plus a key take-away; remain legible in black and white (markers/line styles as well as colour).
  > - Float budget (answering the outline): up to 6 figures plus 2 tables in the main text; the outline's Figs 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and Tables 1–2 fit.
